newDescription:
In this Year 5 / L2 Maths lesson, pupils learn how to read and write Roman numerals, understand the rules for combining symbols, and apply those rules to larger numbers and dates.

This lesson includes:
✔ Learning the seven Roman numeral symbols I, V, X, L, C, D and M and their values
✔ Understanding that Roman numerals have no symbol for zero
✔ Building numbers using addition and subtraction rules
✔ Knowing which symbols may repeat and which may not
✔ Understanding that I, X, C and M can repeat up to three times, while V, L and D cannot repeat
✔ Reading subtractive forms such as IV, IX, XL, XC, CD and CM
✔ Reading additive forms such as VI, LX and DC
✔ Understanding why symbol order matters
✔ Converting between Roman numerals and ordinary numbers
✔ Reading and writing larger Roman numerals into the thousands
✔ Applying Roman numerals to years and historical dates
✔ Using memory clues to remember the larger-value symbols

Pupils begin by learning the seven symbols and their values before exploring the main formation rules. They practise deciding when values should be added and when a smaller symbol before a larger one means subtraction.

The lesson then develops fluency with larger Roman numerals by breaking them into parts, converting numbers in both directions, and checking whether symbol order is valid. Pupils also explore why V, L and D are not repeated and why there is no Roman numeral for zero.

Later activities apply Roman numerals to real and imaginary dates, including years from history and modern life, so pupils can use the rules in meaningful contexts.

By the end of the lesson, learners will be able to read and write Roman numerals confidently, explain the main construction rules, and convert between Roman numerals and ordinary numbers.
